matches.label: Stranraer 2-0 Kelty Hearts (29 Aug, Away)
matches.sourceNote: Real match, 29 August 2026, a 2-0 away defeat - Kelty's only shutout loss in this set. Lewis Dobbie scored both goals for Stranraer, both reported as first-half strikes; exact minutes weren't independently confirmed in the sources found, so 20' and 38' are placeholders within the reported first-half window, not verified to-the-minute. Substitutions, by contrast, ARE well-sourced here - Kelty's full off/on list and minutes are confirmed by Kelty Hearts' own match report (keltyhearts.co.uk, 'Dobbie doubler downs Kelty at Stranraer'), consistent across independent searches.

matches.label: Kelty Hearts 2-1 Annan Athletic (5 Sept, League Two)
matches.sourceNote: Real match, 5 September 2026, a 2-1 win. Full Kelty substitution list confirmed via ESPN's match page (Nathan Lawson for Innes Murray, Kallum Higginbotham for Jamie Hislop, Callum Hannah for Robbie Cole, Gordon Walker for Thomas Falconer) - correcting an earlier version of this file, which wrongly implied Lawson scored moments after coming on. Lawson's 67th-minute introduction is independently well-corroborated; the other three are placed around 75' to match separately-reported detail of a triple change switching to a back five, but that specific minute isn't confirmed to the number. Tommy Muir's equaliser for Annan is placed at ~83' per local press. Goal/sub minutes are reasonable placements within reported windows except where noted, not verified to-the-second.

matches.label: Cumbernauld Colts 0-3 Kelty Hearts (8 Sept, KDM Trophy)
matches.sourceNote: Real match, 8 September 2026, a 3-0 away win. Goal minutes corrected via ESPN's scoreboard listing: Hislop scored in the 3rd and 4th minutes (not 12th/30th as an earlier version of this file had it), Flatman in the 90+3 stoppage-time minute (not 80th). Substitutions came directly from ESPN's match page, relayed by hand: McManus for Ferguson (62'), Flatman for J. Brydon (62'), Murray for Hislop (63', consistent with Hislop's early brace and a second-half withdrawal), Cole for Higginbotham (70'). Jack Brydon is a name already established elsewhere in this project (he conceded the penalty in the Stirling Albion match), good corroborating context. One open question, flagged rather than guessed: ESPN's scoreboard credits the third goal to 'Z. Flatman' while the 62nd-minute substitute was relayed as 'C. Flatman' - possibly an initial mismatch for the same player, possibly two different Flatmans (siblings do turn up together in academy squads). Shown here as plain 'Flatman', no initial asserted, until confirmed.
